answer.narration:
"Juno. The strut's on me. Loose regolith slid under the port pad, and I put her down a hand's width too hard. The medicine's inside, though, and nothing else is bent."

The line goes quiet. Then a short laugh. "The last guy told me the pad moved. You're the first one who didn't lie." The comm pings: three hundred credits, all of it. "I'm sending a crawler with a spare strut. You'll fly her home tomorrow."

She pauses. "Listen. The ridge hab wants a contract pilot who can put down on that ledge every week. It's steady money. There's also a bigger job I don't take, a salvage run in the deep belt. It pays like a ship. Interested?"
choices: Ask about the deep belt salvage run
Ask why Juno won't take it
answer.summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot, wants forty thousand credits to buy Marta Okafor's Kestrel. His job on Dren Vasko's tug Grubstake turned out to be people smuggling. He alerted customs, disabled the drive, got Vasko to surrender, freed eleven refugees and filed an informant claim, though any payout is months away. He flew Juno Reyes's medicine run to Occator Ridge and broke the skiff's weak strut on landing, then owned up to it. Juno paid him in full and is sending a spare strut. She also offered him a weekly ridge contract or a high-paying deep belt salvage run that she won't fly herself.
